subject: GPU pool recommendation, throughput guarantees & tiered-commit ask - SparkWave
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@sparkwave.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial sizing details + ask for committed pricing

Irene — thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick traffic projection and wanted your recommendation on a reserved commit. High level details:
- Production start: Aug 1 (pilot in July)
- Peak concurrent users: ~1,200 (chat agents)
- Avg requests/sec (endpoints): 180 RPS (peaks up to 250 RPS)
- Typical prompt + response context length: 900-1,200 tokens (median ~1,000)
- Model: 13B open variant with quantize95; we expect to run reranking workflows occasionally (small batch jobs)

Our procurement lead also asked if you can provide a 12-month committed capacity price with a tiered discount if we increase to a 24-month commit. Any GPU pool sizing guidance and SLA guarantees you'd recommend for that profile?

Thanks — attaching a simple CSV of expected hourly traffic.

--
Alex Carter
Head of ML Platform, SparkWave
alex.carter@sparkwave.ai
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@sparkwave.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing details + ask for committed pricing

Alex — appreciate the details and the CSV. High-level: we can provide a committed GPU pool with throughput SLAs and a tiered discount structure for 12/24-month terms.

Quick ask before I give a firm recommendation: can you confirm expected p95 latency target (token-level)? Is 95th < 200ms acceptable for interactive chat, or do you need lower? Also, how important is spatial redundancy (multi-region failover) for you?

I looped in Marcus for pricing and Dylan for the sizing math — Dylan will sketch the recommended pool and utilization plan. We'll aim to propose 12- and 24-month pricing bands with credits and an on-ramp option.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Alex Carter <alex.carter@sparkwave.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing details + ask for committed pricing

On Thu, Jun 10, 2027 at 11:03 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — appreciate the details and the CSV. High-level: we can provide...

Alex — I ran a quick workload model based on the numbers you provided and a 13B quantized model profile. Key assumptions: median context 1,000 tokens, average generated tokens per request ~250, batchable prefix reuse 30% (conservative), and quantization to int8-ish performance curve.

Estimated steady-state throughput: ~180 RPS -> token throughput ~ (1000+250)*180 = ~225k tokens/sec (gross). With caching & batching we expect effective reduction to ~160k tokens/sec.

GPU recommendation options (tradeoffs simplified):
1) Latency-optimized: 8x H100 dedicated (NVLink)
   - Target: p95 token latency <120ms for 1k context
   - Peak headroom to 250 RPS with small batching
   - Best for UX-sensitive chat
2) Cost-optimized with quantization & batching: 6x H100 (aggressive quant + KV cache)
   - p95 ~160–220ms, works if 95th < 250ms is acceptable
   - Allows ~20% lower commit price vs option 1
3) Hybrid pool (6x H100 + burst pool access)
   - Base commit sized for 180 RPS; burst to additional nodes for peak days
   - Good if you want lower committed spend with soft guarantees

Operational notes:
- We can define throughput SLOs per-route and auto-fallback to a smaller model variant if capacity constrained.
- For reranking batches, we recommend a small dedicated queue on the pool (2x GPUs) to avoid contention with interactive traffic.

I'll attach the sizing workbook (sparkwave_sizing_v1.xlsx) with the token-level math. Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk through the numbers.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@sparkwave.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@sparkwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing details + ask for committed pricing

Alex — pricing options below (all USD, monthly equivalent shown as guidance). We softened language for negotiation and included credits for onboarding and a one-time migration assist.

Proposed pricing bands (committed GPU pool):
- 12-month commit (6x H100 base pool): $120,000 / month (effective per-GPU blended)
   - Includes 99.5% uptime SLA, 95th-percentile throughput target defined in SOW
   - Onboarding credit: $25k one-time
- 24-month commit (6x H100): $100,000 / month (16% discount vs 12mo)
   - Additional 10% off if customer commits to 2-year prepay
- Latency-optimized 8x H100 option: $155,000 / month (12mo), $135,000 / month (24mo)

Add-ons / optional terms:
- Burst capacity (pay-as-you-go) available at market rate for extra GPUs during peaks
- Dedicated reranking queue reservation: $5,000 / month (reserves 2 GPUs)
- Enhanced retention for trace logs and audit: $3,000 / month

If Procurement wants to reduce near-term spend without losing performance, the hybrid pool (6x commit + burst) is a common path. We can structure a ramp: 6 months at the 12-month rate, then convert to 24-month at an agreed uplift.

Next steps: if you want to move forward I can send a proposed term sheet (DocuSign link) with the 12- and 24-month options and a short SOW that pins throughput SLOs per route.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@sparkwave.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@sparkwave.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing details + ask for committed pricing

Thanks — helpful breakdown. A couple quick asks from procurement before we commit:
1) Can you share a written SLA for the 99.5% uptime and what credits look like for missed targets?
2) If we do the 24-month path, can we get a deeper discount if we agree to a $2M total committed spend (prepay) vs monthly billing?
3) For the hybrid option: can you guarantee burst availability for scheduled campaign windows?

We prefer the 6x H100 base commit if the p95 is within 200ms; that aligns with our UX bar. Also please include the reranking queue as part of the proposal as a single line item.

Appreciate it — can you send the DocuSign term sheet and SOW so our procurement/legal can review?

--
Alex
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@sparkwave.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing details + ask for committed pricing

Alex — noted. Marcus: I think we can confirm the following before sending the term sheet:
- Provide a concise SLA summary (uptime, credits calc) and include a clause for scheduled bursts (we can guarantee capacity for pre-scheduled windows; ad-hoc bursts are best-effort)
- For $2M prepay over 24 months we can offer an additional 8% off the 24-month rate (i.e., stackable on the 24mo discount with Finance sign-off)
- Include the reranking queue line item ($5k/mo) in the term sheet and a 30-day onboarding credit

I'll upload the term sheet and SOW to DocuSign and share the link. Expect the draft in the next 24 hours. If you'd like, we can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk procurement through SLA and burst mechanics.

Thanks — attaching the proposed term sheet (redwood_proposed_term_sheet_v2.pdf) to the record.

Best,
Irene
